::: {#def-vector-derivative}
#### Vector derivative
If $f(\vb)$ is a scalar-valued function of a $p \times 1$ vector $\vb$,
such as $f(\vb) = \tp{\vx}\vb$,
then its **vector derivative** is:

$$
\deriv{ \vb} f(\vb) =
\sbmat{
\deriv{\beta_1}f(\vb) \\
\deriv{\beta_2}f(\vb) \\
\vdots \\
\deriv{\beta_p}f(\vb)
}
$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-vector-derivative}
#### A vector derivative

Let $\vb = \tp{(\beta_1, \beta_2)}$ and $f(\vb) = 3 \beta_1 + 5 \beta_2^2$. Then

$$
\underbrace{\deriv{\vb} f(\vb)}_{2 \times 1}
= \sbmat{
\deriv{\beta_1} (3 \beta_1 + 5 \beta_2^2) \\
\deriv{\beta_2} (3 \beta_1 + 5 \beta_2^2)
}
= \sbmat{ 3 \\ 10 \beta_2 },
$$

and at $\vb = \tp{(1, 2)}$ the vector derivative is $\tp{(3, 20)}$.

:::
